questions.prompt: Explain what “water of crystallisation” means, using copper sulfate as an example.
questions.modelAnswer: Water of crystallisation is the fixed number of water molecules chemically combined in each formula unit of a salt in its crystals. Blue copper sulfate is CuSO₄·5H₂O: five water molecules per unit. Heating removes this water, leaving white anhydrous CuSO₄; adding water turns it blue again.
rubric: Fixed number of water molecules in the crystal
